name: Citron Green
lede: Citron Green is a moderate greenish yellow named for the citron, a fragrant citrus fruit, recorded in Ridgway's 1912 color standard and again by Maerz and Paul in 1930.

sections.title: Named for a fruit, not a color family
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* lists Citron Green on plate XXXI, hue 25′′, tone b [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 places it in block 102, moderate greenish yellow, 4.2 units from that block's centroid, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 *A Dictionary of Color* records the same name on their plate 19 K 2 [2]. Two near-duplicates sit within 2.5 units of it in our library, Light Greenish Yellow and Pale Greenish Yellow, both also from Ridgway and the ISCC-NBS [2]. The nearest distinct named color is [[khaki]], 2.6 units away [2].

The citron is a citrus fruit grown mainly for its thick, fragrant rind rather than its juice, and the color borrows its pale yellow-green skin rather than its flesh [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Citron Green covers at least five per cent of the canvas in 628 of them, about 2.6 per cent, as photographed [3]. It is strongest by far in Kalighat painting, 51 of 96 works, over 20 times the archive rate, and common across Indian painting generally, 61 of 721 works [3]. It plays a highlight in 92 per cent of its appearances and peaks in paintings from the 1890s [3]. These counts are museum photographs of aged, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [3].
